subtopics.title: Protections, Exclusions and CBAM
subtopics.summary: Both sides keep negative lists of sensitive farm goods to protect rural livelihoods and food security. A parallel agreement protects geographical indications such as Darjeeling Tea and Champagne. The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism applies a carbon levy on selected imports from 1 January 2026, and India received a most-favoured-nation assurance on it without a full exemption.
facts: India's exclusions: dairy, wheat, rice and poultry
EU's exclusions: beef, sugar and rice
Geographical indication protection for Darjeeling Tea and Champagne
EUR 500 million pledged for decarbonisation of Indian industries
CBAM full implementation with carbon levy from 1 January 2026
Transitional phase 2023-2025 involved reporting only, with no financial levy
CBAM sectors: cement, aluminium, fertilisers, iron and steel, hydrogen, electricity
CBAM certificate price linked to the EU ETS carbon price
Credit allowed if a carbon tax was already paid in the exporting country
India got an MFN assurance on CBAM but no full exemption

subtopics.title: 2030 Roadmap and the US Factor
subtopics.summary: The 'Towards 2030' Joint India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda is a five-year framework adopted at the 16th Summit to move ties beyond trade. It is organised into pillars covering prosperity, technology, security, connectivity, and enablers such as skills and mobility. The deal is also framed as a hedge against US tariff policy, after 50% reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods were imposed in August 2025.
facts: Official title: 'Towards 2030: Joint India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda'
A five-year framework adopted at the 16th India-EU Summit
Prosperity and Sustainability pillar includes green hydrogen and carbon market alignment
Technology and Innovation pillar includes Trade and Technology Council and 6G, semiconductors, quantum
Security and Defence pillar focuses on maritime security in the Indo-Pacific
Connectivity pillar includes IMEC and the EU's Global Gateway initiative
Enablers pillar covers skills and mobility, with a European Legal Gateway in India
Mutual recognition of professional qualifications targeted by 2030
50% reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods imposed in August 2025
Described as creating a 'Third Pole' in global trade

subtopics.title: EU Basics and India-EU Ties
subtopics.summary: The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states, and it traces its origins to the European Coal and Steel Community formed in 1951 by six countries. Its key institutions include the Commission, Parliament, Council, Court of Justice and the European Central Bank. India and the EU have had diplomatic relations since 1962, and ties were upgraded to a Strategic Partnership in 2004.
facts: EU is a political and economic union of 27 member states
Began as the European Coal and Steel Community (1951) with six founding members
European Commission: executive body that proposes laws and manages the budget
European Parliament: the EU's only elected legislative body
European Council: heads of state or government, sets political direction
Court of Justice of the EU ensures uniform application of EU law
Diplomatic relations with the European Economic Community established in 1962
Upgraded to a Strategic Partnership at The Hague Summit in 2004
EU is India's largest trading partner in goods and largest foreign investor
Bilateral trade in 2024-25 was $136.53 billion
